status: For Sky's yes (brief 102, Fable 2026-11-08). Nothing here is in text.json: the sweep applies only after the yes.

rows.who: The Fixer, to the person's face after a no
before: You said no. You'll remember me.
All right. Next time, we'll have to offer more.
No, then. You'll want more next time.
after: Of course. Forget I asked.
Then we'll say no more about it.
That's all right. I won't keep you.
rows.why: Your own example, and two lines reciting the rule that a later offer costs more. She bows out, as a gracious stranger would; the Refused before chip carries the rest.

rows.who: The Fixer, after someone takes fright and means to report her
before: You're reporting us, then. I understand.
So you're reporting our talk. We'll leave it there.
All right. I hear you're reporting this.
after: I'm sorry. I've misjudged you.
Then I'll go. No harm meant.
I see. We'll leave you in peace.
rows.why: Each line read the outcome back to the person's face. The report plate on the HUD already shows it on its way.

rows.who: The Fixer, after a too-small offer is turned down
before: Too little, then. Let me listen first.
Fair enough. I'll learn what it takes.
Not enough. I should have known more first.
after: I'm sorry. I didn't mean it as an insult.
Forgive me. I should have known better.
I understand. I'm sorry to have bothered you.
rows.why: Told the player what to do next (Listen first), out loud, to Inez's face. The Listen first chip says it.

rows.who: The Fixer, when someone is warmer but not won
before: Not yet, then. I'll come back.
Let me help once more. Then we'll talk.
I'll come back. You still need another hand.
after: Think it over. There's no hurry.
Take your time. I'll look in again.
Keep it in mind. We can talk another day.
rows.why: "Help once more" and "another hand" recite the rule. She can still say she'll call again: that is her own intent.

rows.who: Inez, helped again (in it for the money)
before: Still good for it. I'll remember.
More? I could get used to this.
after: Still paying? You're my favourite customer.
More? I could get used to this.
rows.why: Your "I will remember you" family. The second line already works, so it stays.

rows.who: Inez, helped again (frightened)
before: You've paid it? I feel no safer.
Thank you. I won't forget this.
after: You've paid it? I feel no safer.
Thank you. You don't know what this means.
rows.why: "I won't forget" is the same family: the game remembers, and she needn't say so.

rows.who: The driver, helped again (loyal to his post)
before: Reliable of you. I'll note that.
A steady friend. I won't forget.
after: Reliable of you. I'm grateful.
A steady friend. Thank you.
rows.why: Both lines promise memory.

rows.who: The guard, helped again (loyal)
before: That settles my trouble. Thank you, citizen.
You've put it right again. I won't forget it.
after: That settles my trouble. Thank you, citizen.
You've put it right again. I'm in your debt.
rows.why: Same family. His thanks stays.

rows.who: A passer-by who saw who fired
before: I saw who fired.
I'll remember that face.
I saw it all. Every bit.
after: That one! That's who fired!
Did you see? Right there, with the gun!
I saw it. I saw the whole thing!
rows.why: These lines existed to tell the player the witness can name the shooter later. A frightened passer-by points and shouts; the game keeps what they saw.

rows.who: The guard, who saw who fired
before: I saw the shooter. I'll know him.
I saw who fired. Noted.
after: There! That's the shooter!
I saw that! Stop right there!
rows.why: "I'll know him" and "Noted" are the memory rule. He shouts, as a guard would.

rows.who: The guard, turning down a free favour (in it for the money)
before: No free favours. Next time, my fee goes up.
No. My next favour costs extra now you've asked.
after: No free favours on this door, friend.
Not for nothing, I don't. Move along.
rows.why: Both recite the rule that a refusal makes the next offer dearer.

rows.who: The guard, warmed but not won (loyal)
before: Help me once more. Then I'll return the favour.
One more kindness, and I'll make an exception for you.
after: Kind of you, citizen. I'll think on it.
Very kind. But I've a post to think of.
rows.why: Both state the not-yet rule word for word: one more Help turns him.

rows.who: The driver, warmed but not won (loyal)
before: Generous. I need a moment to decide.
A little more, and I'm yours.
after: Generous. I need a moment to decide.
Let me sleep on it, friend.
rows.why: "A little more, and I'm yours" is the rule. His first line already holds.

rows.who: Inez, alarmed by a stranger's help (loyal)
before: Even a favour gets reported, I'm afraid.
Kind or not, I have to write it down.
after: No, thank you. The owner wouldn't like it.
Who sent you? I think you should go.
rows.why: Both state the rule that a loyal person reports any approach. She refuses and wants them gone; the report plate shows the rest.

rows.who: The driver, offered a bribe (loyal)
before: I report bribes. Even polite ones.
Keep that. This goes in my log.
after: Keep that. I drive for the Councillor.
Money? On the Office's own step?
rows.why: The first recites a rule, the second announces the report.

rows.who: The guard, paid (in it for the money)
before: That's good money. Call when you want the favour.
For that bonus, I'll oblige when you call.
after: That's good money. Consider me obliged.
For that, I'll see you right.
rows.why: Both teach a Call, and the guard has none: the scene's card says there is nothing to call him for yet.

rows.who: A passer-by who goes over to look
before: I'll look first, then tell the police.
Let me check before I report it.
I'd better look before I call the police.
after: Hello? Are you all right down there?
Is that someone? Hold on, let me look.
Oh dear. Can you hear me?
rows.why: Each line narrated the witness's choice as a two-step plan. People go and look; the report plate shows when they head off.

rows.who: A passer-by going for a telephone
before: I'm going to find a telephone and call the police.
I need a phone to tell the police.
I'll get to a telephone and report this.
after: Where's a telephone? Somebody needs the police!
Police! Somebody find me a telephone!
There's a call box. Stay with them!
rows.why: The report's route read out like a procedure. Shouted, they are what a person says as they run.

rows.who: Inez on the telephone, when the guard has already come once
before: He's been once this shift. He won't come again.
Sorry, one visit a shift. He's had his.
after: He's been once this shift. He won't come again.
I've had him over once already. He won't risk it twice.
rows.why: "One visit a shift" recites the rule as if it were café policy. Her first line gives her reason and stays.

rows.who: The guard, running in at the car
before: Armed men! Not in my square!
Rivals! I'll cover you!
after: Armed men! Not in my square!
Get down, all of you! Guns!
rows.why: He has never seen the cell, and nobody outside it knows the other crew as rivals.

rows.who: The Fixer's offer in Inez's Ask scenes (seven scenes, first variant)
before: Could you do me a small favour? I can't pay.
after: Could you do me a small favour? It's nothing much.
rows.why: "I can't pay" reads out what Ask means. Nobody asking a favour says so.

rows.who: Inez's last line when she takes the full Help (also help-inez-2-known)
before: Then I'm with you. I watch that square all day, and if trouble's coming for you, I'll find a way to warn you.
after: Then I'm with you. Whatever this is, please be careful.
rows.why: It announces a feature: helped, she warns the cell at the car. Unannounced, her shout of "Careful! Men by the car!" comes as a surprise that her kindness earned.
